quadratics.description:
Be able to answer any Quadratics question on Paper 1 without notes.

Key points:
• Complete the square and read off the vertex and line of symmetry
• Use the discriminant b² − 4ac for two, one or no real roots
• Solve quadratic inequalities with a sketch
• Solve a linear and a quadratic equation simultaneously
• Solve equations that are quadratic in a function of x, e.g. in x² or √x
• Use the discriminant for a line that is tangent to a curve

How: For each key point, rework one example from your notes or textbook, then cover the answer and do it again from memory. Write down any formula you had to look up.

First step: Open your notes on Quadratics and redo one example for the first key point without looking.

mapped.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry (9701), Paper 2
units: Atomic structure: Describe protons, neutrons and electrons and define atomic and mass numbers; Define isotopes and explain why they have the same chemical properties
Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry: Define relative atomic, isotopic, molecular and formula masses; Use the mole and the Avogadro constant in calculations
Chemical bonding: Describe ionic bonding and the structure and properties of ionic lattices; Describe metallic bonding and its link to properties
States of matter: State assumptions of the kinetic model of an ideal gas; Use pV = nRT to find amount, pressure, volume or temperature
Chemical energetics: Define enthalpy change of reaction, formation, combustion and neutralisation; Draw and use enthalpy profile diagrams showing activation energy
Electrochemistry (redox): Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer and oxidation number; Deduce oxidation numbers of elements in compounds and ions
Equilibria: Describe dynamic equilibrium in reversible reactions; Apply Le Chatelier's principle to changes in concentration, pressure and temperature
Reaction kinetics: Define rate of reaction and describe methods of measuring it; Explain effects of concentration, pressure, particle size and temperature on rate

The Periodic Table: chemical periodicity: Describe trends in atomic radius, ionic radius and ionisation energy across Period 3; Describe the reactions of Period 3 elements with oxygen, chlorine and water
Group 2: Describe trends in atomic radius, ionisation energy and reactivity down Group 2; Describe reactions of Group 2 metals with oxygen, water and acids
Group 17: Describe trends in colour, volatility and reactivity of the halogens; Describe displacement reactions of halogens and halide ions
Nitrogen and sulfur: Describe the bonding and structure of nitrogen and its lack of reactivity; Describe the reactions of ammonia as a base and as a ligand

An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry: Name organic compounds using IUPAC rules and draw displayed, structural and skeletal formulae; Identify functional groups: alkane, alkene, halogeno, hydroxyl, carbonyl, carboxyl, ester, amide, nitrile
Hydrocarbons: Describe the alkanes, their free-radical substitution with halogens and its mechanism; Explain the relative reactivity of primary, secondary and tertiary hydrogen atoms
Halogen compounds: Classify halogenoalkanes as primary, secondary or tertiary; Describe nucleophilic substitution with OH-, CN- and NH3, with mechanism

Hydroxy compounds: Classify alcohols as primary, secondary and tertiary and describe industrial ethanol production; Describe combustion and oxidation of alcohols with different reagents and conditions
Carbonyl compounds: Identify aldehydes and ketones and name them; Describe oxidation of aldehydes but not ketones and the tests used
Carboxylic acids and derivatives: Describe the acidity of carboxylic acids and reactions with metals, bases and carbonates; Describe reduction of carboxylic acids to primary alcohols
Nitrogen compounds: Describe the structure of primary amines and their basicity; Describe formation of amines from halogenoalkanes with ammonia
Polymerisation: Describe addition polymerisation of alkenes and draw repeat units; Relate the properties and uses of addition polymers to their structure
Organic synthesis: Design multi-step routes using the reactions of the AS functional groups; Select reagents and conditions for each step

Analytical techniques: Explain the principles and use of infra-red spectroscopy and identify functional groups from absorptions; Describe mass spectrometry and determine molecular mass from the molecular ion
